description.value: The study investigated regional brain activation associated with cue-elicited craving and resisting the urge to smoke in treatment-seeking nicotine-dependent smokers, including differences associated with specific resistance strategies.

spans.text: In the current study, we utilized fMRI and smoking-related cues to further investigate regional brain activation in nicotine-dependent smokers during craving and when attempting to resist the urge to smoke while being presented smoking-related cues.

design.value: A block-design fMRI study in which nicotine-dependent smokers viewed smoking-related and neutral images during separate Crave and Resist scans, with smoking-related cues, neutral cues, and rest blocks.

spans.text: Stimuli were presented in a block design using standardized pictures of people smoking or engaged in neutral activities matched in frequency and gender adapted from previous alcohol cue reactivity studies conducted by our research group.

During the scanning session, participants underwent two back to back fMRI stimuli presentation during the scanning session with the instruction to “allow yourself to crave when you see the smoking related pictures,” followed by a second stimuli presentation with the instructions to “resist the urge to smoke when you see the smoking pictures by any means you find helpful.”

task_name.value: smoking-related cue reactivity with craving and resisting craving

spans.text: In the current study, we utilized fMRI and smoking-related cues to further investigate regional brain activation in nicotine-dependent smokers during craving and when attempting to resist the urge to smoke while being presented smoking-related cues.

task_description.value: Participants viewed blocks of smoking-related images, neutral images, and rest, first instructed to allow themselves to crave and then instructed to resist the urge to smoke.

spans.text: Each epoch contained three, 24 second blocks: 1 block of smoking related images, 1 block of neutral images, and 1 block of rest with a static crosshair.

During the scanning session, participants underwent two back to back fMRI stimuli presentation during the scanning session with the instruction to “allow yourself to crave when you see the smoking related pictures,” followed by a second stimuli presentation with the instructions to “resist the urge to smoke when you see the smoking pictures by any means you find helpful.”

stimuli.value: Standardized pictures of people smoking or engaged in neutral activities, smoking-related objects, and matched neutral objects.

spans.text: Stimuli were presented in a block design using standardized pictures of people smoking or engaged in neutral activities matched in frequency and gender adapted from previous alcohol cue reactivity studies conducted by our research group.
Objects related to smoking (packages of cigarettes, ashtrays, etc.) matched with neutral objects (pencils, dishes, etc) for the control condition were included.
Each block was followed by a 6 second screen with a self-rating of craving using a hand-pad fitted on to the right hand.

spans.text: FSL pre-statistics processing prior to analysis included: removal of non-brain with Brain Extraction Tool (BET) (Smith, 2002), motion correction with Motion Correction FMRIB Linear Image Registration Tool (MCFLIRT) (Jenkinson et al., 2002), spatial smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of FWHM 8 mm, and grand-mean intensity normalization of the entire 4D dataset by a single multiplicative factor; highpass temporal filtering (Gaussian-weighted least-squares straight line fitting, with sigma=50.0s).

The following contrasts were tested during the Crave and Resist Condition: “smoking-related cues minus neutral cues,” “neutral cues minus smoking-related cues”, “smoking-related Crave minus smoking-related Resist” and finally “smoking-related Resist minus smoking-related Crave”.

During the Crave condition, utilizing mixed effects analysis (Z>2.3 and corrected cluster thresholded at p=.05) the left ACC, medial PFC, bilateral middle OFC, bilateral PCC, bilateral precuneus, and left middle cingulate were activated when comparing the smoking related cues to the neutral cues (Table 1 and Figure 2).
